rounds.text: Jigar Cables Ltd is demonstrably under-appreciated when evaluated through intrinsic valuation models, trading at ₹ 65.0 against a DCF intrinsic value of ₹ 81 per share, which provides a tangible margin of safety of 19.7% [E2, E39, E40]. This conservative valuation is further highlighted by a reverse DCF showing the current price implies only 14.9% earnings growth, trailing the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E41]. Long-term compounding metrics reinforce the fundamental strength of the business, evidenced by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 32% and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 34% [E14, E17]. These robust fundamentals have noticeably outpaced stock performance, with 5-year profit growth exceeding the 21% share price growth, indicating that the market is lagging behind the company's operational expansion [E20, E42]. Recent operating metrics show positive momentum, including a quarterly operating margin expansion of two percentage points year-over-year to 6% in March 2026 alongside an increasing trend over the last four quarters [E27, E29]. Furthermore, operational efficiency has strengthened notably through an improvement in debtor days from 40.1 to 19.6 days, supported by a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 2.86x [E34, E45]. Conceded: [E8], [E9], [E10], [E11], [E12], [E13], [E16], [E19], [E22], [E26], [E30], [E31], [E32], [E35], [E46], [E47], [E48], [E54], [E55].

Jigar Cables Ltd presents a concerning financial profile characterized by deteriorating cash flows and inefficient capital utilization. The company reported negative operating cash flow of Rs -1.43 Cr and a severe free cash flow deficit of Rs -16.24 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32]. This is compounded by a cash conversion ratio of -0.79x, indicating that reported profits are not translating into actual liquidity [E30]. Furthermore, the company’s profitability metrics consistently underperform sector benchmarks, with an ROE of 7.02% and ROCE of 8.54% falling well short of the sector averages of 10.87% and 12.93%, respectively [E9, E10]. The valuation appears stretched, as the stock trades at a P/E of 30x, which is a premium to the sector benchmark of 21.43x, despite the company’s recent 45% decline in compounded sales growth [E6, E16]. Conceded: the company has maintained a comfortable current ratio of 2.86x and has demonstrated historical compounded sales growth of 32% over five years [E14, E34]. Nevertheless, the combination of rising debt—which jumped from Rs 2.83 Cr to Rs 11.93 Cr in one year—and the absence of any dividend payout suggests significant risks for shareholders [E35, E46].

While the bull leans heavily on a DCF intrinsic value of ₹ 81 and a 19.7% margin of safety, this model output ignores severe current operational deterioration, including a trailing twelve month sales growth collapse of -45% and a profit growth contraction of -1% [E16, E19, E39, E40]. The bull's reliance on historical 5-year sales and profit compounding of 32% and 34% masks a deteriorating present, evidenced by a negative operating cash flow of Rs -1.43 Cr and an alarming free cash flow burn of Rs -16.24 Cr in March 2026 [E14, E17, E31, E32]. Furthermore, the claim of strong operational efficiency ignores that cash conversion stands at a deeply negative -0.79x, and borrowings have spiked sharply from Rs 2.83 Cr to Rs 11.93 Cr in a single year alongside concerning signals that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E30, E35, E48]. Conceded: [E27], [E29], [E34], [E41], [E45].
